prompt: What are the maximum lengths of a copper permanent link and of a channel?
correct: 90 m permanent link, 100 m channel
explanation: The permanent link is the fixed cabling (up to 90 m); the channel adds the patch and equipment cords (100 m total).
quote: The maximum permitted length of the permanent link is 90 meters.

prompt: Why certify the permanent link instead of only testing the channel?
correct: Good patch cords can hide a bad link, and cords get moved
options: Good patch cords can hide a bad link, and cords get moved
Channel testing is not allowed on new installations
The permanent link test is faster to fail
Patch cords are never part of a real network
explanation: With very high quality patch cords a channel can pass even though the fixed link underneath has failed.
quote: if very high. Quality patch cords are used, the channel can pass even if the permanent link has failed

prompt: What does a PASS* (pass with an asterisk) on a copper certification tester mean?
correct: The result is within the tester's accuracy of the limit: a pass under the standard, but check the project rule
options: The result is within the tester's accuracy of the limit: a pass under the standard, but check the project rule
The link failed and must be re-terminated
The link was tested to the wrong category
explanation: Marginal results still pass under TIA and ISO/IEC unless it was agreed in writing that they are unacceptable.
quote: According to TIA and ISO/IEC standards, any marginal pass is still considered a pass and compliant.

prompt: What are the minimum bend radius and the maximum pulling tension for 4-pair UTP cable?
correct: 4 x the cable OD; 25 lbf (110 N)
options: 4 x the cable OD; 25 lbf (110 N)
explanation: Over-bending or over-pulling distorts the pair geometry; the damage is invisible but shows up in certification.
quote: ANSI/TIA-568.2-D limits 4-pair copper cable to 25 pounds-force, or 110 newtons.

prompt: What is the maximum untwist at a Cat6 termination?
options: No limit, as long as the pins are right
explanation: Excessive untwisting is one of the most common causes of NEXT failures.
quote: No more than 13 millimetres, or half an inch, from the termination point per ANSI/TIA-568.2-D.

prompt: What is the maximum spacing between J-hooks?
explanation: The spacing limit exists to control sag; 4 to 5 ft is typical.
quote: The hard ceiling on spacing is 5 feet (60 inches) between supports.

prompt: What must happen before a firestopped penetration is covered up?
correct: Check the listed system matches the detail; inspect, photograph and log it
options: Check the listed system matches the detail; inspect, photograph and log it
Nothing: firestop is inspected at the end of the project
Paint over it so it matches the wall
Remove the product labels so the finish looks clean
explanation: Firestop systems must not be concealed before they are inspected and approved.
quote: Firestop systems must not be concealed from view before being inspected and approved

prompt: Within a 100 m copper channel, how much of the length may be patch cords?
correct: No more than 10 m
options: Any length, as long as the total stays under 100 m
explanation: Up to 90 m of cabling plus no more than 10 m of patch cords.
quote: Industry standards limit the overall length of a channel to 100 meters, including up to 90 meters of cabling and no more than 10 meters of patch cords.

prompt: What is the permanent link in a copper cabling system?
correct: The fixed portion of the channel, such as patch panel to work area outlet
options: The fixed portion of the channel, such as patch panel to work area outlet
The patch cord from the switch to the patch panel
The equipment cord from the outlet to the laptop
The whole path including both active devices
explanation: The channel adds the cords; the permanent link is what stays in the wall.
quote: The permanent link is the fixed portion of the channel up to 90 meters.

prompt: How must a marginal test result be marked on a certification report?
correct: With an asterisk (*)
options: It must be deleted from the report
explanation: The asterisk shows that tester accuracy plays a role in the result.
quote: marginal test results for a parameter shall be marked with an asterisk (*)

prompt: A tester lets you switch off the asterisk so marginal results look like clean passes. Such a tester is:
correct: Non-compliant
options: Compliant if the firmware is current
explanation: Hiding marginal results breaks the standard and puts the installer's reputation at risk.
quote: Any tester that allows you to disable the asterisk and hide marginal results is non-compliant

prompt: When does a marginal pass (PASS*) NOT count as a pass?
correct: When it was specified and agreed in writing that marginal results are unacceptable
options: When it was specified and agreed in writing that marginal results are unacceptable
Always: an asterisk is a fail
When the link is shorter than 15 m
explanation: Agree on how marginal results are treated before testing starts.
quote: Unless it was specified and agreed upon in writing that marginal test results are unacceptable, your marginal passes still pass.

prompt: Which additional test is required when certifying Category 6A cabling?
correct: Alien Crosstalk
explanation: Alien Crosstalk can stop 10GBASE-T from working, so Cat6A certification includes it.
quote: For Category 6A, Alien Crosstalk testing is also required

prompt: Certification plot data for Category 6 cabling runs up to ____.
correct: 250 MHz
explanation: Cat5e is tested to 100 MHz, Cat6 to 250 MHz, Cat6A to 500 MHz.
quote: up to 100 MHz for Category 5e, 250 MHz for Category 6, and 500 MHz for Category 6A

prompt: A Modular Plug Terminated Link (MPTL) plugs a horizontal cable straight into a device. Which devices is it typically used for?
correct: Devices that do not need to move, such as PoE lights and surveillance cameras
options: Devices that do not need to move, such as PoE lights and surveillance cameras
explanation: Standards allow an MPTL where an outlet plus equipment cord is impractical or unsafe.
quote: ideal for devices that don't typically need to move, such as PoE lights and surveillance cameras

prompt: How is a Modular Plug Terminated Link (for example a camera cable) tested so the field-terminated plug is included?
correct: Permanent link adapter at the near end, patch cord adapter at the far end
options: Permanent link adapter at the near end, patch cord adapter at the far end
No test is needed for a single plug
explanation: A channel adapter at the far end leaves out the mated plug and gives optimistic results.
quote: industry standards require a permanent link adapter at the near end and a patch cord adapter at the far end

prompt: What is the minimum bend radius for shielded twisted-pair cable?
correct: 8 x the cable outer diameter
explanation: Unshielded is 4 x OD; shielded needs at least 8 x OD.
quote: shielded cables require at least eight times

prompt: What minimum separation does TIA-569 give between power and data cabling?
correct: 12 in (about 300 mm)
explanation: Where they must cross, cross at right angles.
quote: ANSI/TIA-569-D specifies a minimum of 12 inches, roughly 300 millimetres, between power and data cabling.

prompt: Data cable has to cross a power cable. How should they cross?
correct: At right angles (90 degrees)
options: Data cable wrapped around the power cable
explanation: Crossing at right angles minimises electromagnetic coupling.
quote: Where they must intersect, cross them at right angles to minimise electromagnetic coupling.

prompt: A Cat5e patch cord is plugged into a new Cat6A channel. Is that acceptable?
correct: No: all components in a channel must be the same performance category
options: No: all components in a channel must be the same performance category
Yes, patch cords do not count
Yes, if the cord is shorter than 1 m
Yes, if it is labeled in red
explanation: The channel performs to its weakest component, and mixing usually voids the warranty.
quote: TIA-568.0-E requires all components within a channel to be of the same performance category.

prompt: BICSI guidance limits bundles to ____ cables or fewer unless the cable is certified for larger bundles.
explanation: Big bundles add alien crosstalk and trap PoE heat.
quote: BICSI guidance is to limit bundles to 24 cables or fewer unless the cable is certified for larger bundles.

prompt: Shielded (STP/FTP) cabling should be bonded:
correct: Bond at one end only
explanation: Bonding both ends can create a ground loop, the interference the shield is meant to prevent.
quote: Bond shielded cabling at one end only.

prompt: Which wiring scheme should be used for copper terminations?
correct: One scheme, T568A or T568B, used consistently across the whole facility
options: One scheme, T568A or T568B, used consistently across the whole facility
T568A at one end and T568B at the other on every link
A different scheme for each floor
explanation: Mixing schemes creates crossed pairs and failed wire maps.
quote: Use one wiring scheme - T568A or T568B - consistently across the whole facility

prompt: How much may cable sag between two J-hooks?
correct: No more than about 12 in
options: Any amount, if the hooks are 5 ft apart
It must be pulled tight with no sag
explanation: Excess sag puts tension on the jacket and can deform the pairs.
quote: Cable should not droop more than about 12 inches between two supports.

prompt: What is the usual fill limit for a J-hook?
correct: About 40% of the hook's cross-sectional area
options: About 40% of the hook's cross-sectional area
explanation: Headroom leaves room for later cable, lets heat out and stops the bottom cables being crushed.
quote: keep fill at or below roughly 40% of the hook's cross-sectional area

prompt: What may J-hooks be attached to?
correct: Real structure such as joists, threaded rod or structural members
options: Real structure such as joists, threaded rod or structural members
explanation: Never hang cable supports from the ceiling grid or other trades' systems.
quote: Land hooks on real structure (joists, threaded rod, structural members), never on ceiling grid wire or other trades' systems.

prompt: Under TIA-606, what must a cable label be?
correct: Legible, permanent, at both ends, and matched to the records
options: Legible, permanent, at both ends, and matched to the records
On the reel, not on the cable
explanation: Each printed identifier links to a record, so anyone can trace the cable later.
quote: Legible Permanent Placed at both ends of cables

prompt: What does TIA-606-C require for each identifier printed on a label?
correct: A linked record for that identifier
options: A linked record for that identifier
explanation: The label and the record together make the infrastructure manageable for moves, adds and changes.
quote: The standard requires you to link a record for each identifier that is printed on a label

prompt: Which tools does the IFC guide list for a firestop inspection?
correct: A flashlight, a measuring device and a cutting tool
options: A flashlight, a measuring device and a cutting tool
A megger and a torque wrench
An OTDR and a launch cable
explanation: Material depth, annular space and product type are measured, and destructive checks are sometimes needed.
quote: Appropriate tools for firestop inspections should include a flashlight, measuring device and cutting tool.

prompt: What rating must a through-penetration firestop system have?
correct: Equal to or greater than the rating of the assembly penetrated
options: Equal to or greater than the rating of the assembly penetrated
At least half the wall's rating
Any rating, as long as it is caulked
explanation: Check the listing against the wall or floor actually penetrated.
quote: Is the rating of the through penetration system equal or greater than the assembly penetrated?

prompt: When is an Engineering Judgment (EJ) needed for firestopping?
correct: When a unique condition has not been tested and does not match a published listing
options: When a unique condition has not been tested and does not match a published listing
Only for penetrations smaller than 1 in
When the installer runs out of the listed product
explanation: EJs must be approved by the building official and available to the field inspector.
quote: since they have not been tested and do not comply with a published design listing

prompt: Where must the construction documents that detail firestop locations and systems be kept?
correct: On site, to support the inspection
options: On site, to support the inspection
They are not needed after approval
explanation: The inspector compares the installed system with the approved details.
quote: Construction documents detailing the firestop locations and systems must be kept on site

prompt: How often should a CCTV camera system get at least basic maintenance (clean domes, check cables)?
correct: At least every six months
explanation: Dirty domes and worn cables quietly ruin image usability.
quote: maintenance should be scheduled at least every six months

prompt: Which statement about camera IP (ingress protection) ratings is true?
correct: IP67 or IP68 is not necessarily more weather-proof than IP66
options: IP67 or IP68 is not necessarily more weather-proof than IP66
Any IP rating means the camera is certified for outdoor use
A higher IP number always means better rain resistance
IP ratings only describe vandal resistance
explanation: The IP66 water-jet test is harsher than IP67's short submersion.
quote: Higher classes (IP67 or IP68) do not indicate better resistance, and an IP67 camera is not necessarily weather-proof.

prompt: A camera only needs to detect that a person entered an area, not identify them. Roughly what pixel density does that need?
correct: About 25 pixels per metre
explanation: Use-case classes (IEC 62676-4) range from monitor and detect up to identify and inspect; identification needs far more pixels on target.
quote: this requires a pixel density of approximately 25 pixels/m throughout the surveillance area

prompt: How do you avoid finding out that a camera has been offline for weeks only when footage is needed?
correct: Have the video management system monitor devices and alert when one goes offline
options: Have the video management system monitor devices and alert when one goes offline
Reboot every camera once a year
Record at a lower frame rate
explanation: Offline cameras go unnoticed if nobody is actively monitoring them.
quote: Many video management systems can actively monitor cameras and other devices, and can send an alert if a device goes offline.
